members.name: Mike Rogers

Passed the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, imposing new sanctions on Iran, Russia, and North Korea for ballistic missile programs, human rights abuses, cyber activities, and other geopolitical reasons.

The bill requires Treasury to report on Iranian officials' assets and recommend additional sanctions to counter ballistic missile development.

The bill expands sanctions on North Korea by targeting individuals and entities involved in significant transactions with North Korea, including those related to coal, iron, textiles, and other sectors. The bill also authorizes the President to designate and subject to sanctions any person who knowingly engages in specified activities with North Korea.
The FY2018 NDAA authorized defense appropriations, including Overseas Contingency Operations funding that supports U.S. military activities abroad.

Passed the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, imposing new sanctions on Iran, Russia, and North Korea for ballistic missile programs, human rights abuses, cyber activities, and other geopolitical reasons.
HR2810 passed, closing portions of the conference on the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018

The House passed the Otto Warmbier North Korea Nuclear Sanctions Act, imposing broad financial sanctions on entities doing business with North Korea and requiring the U.S. to oppose international financial assistance to governments that don't implement similar sanctions.

The House passed the Iran Ballistic Missiles and International Sanctions Enforcement Act, which imposes new sanctions on Iranian government agencies and foreign entities involved in Iran's ballistic missile program and conventional weapons transfers.
The bill requires Treasury to report on Iranian officials' assets and recommend additional sanctions to counter ballistic missile development.

The bill imposes reporting requirements on financial institutions involved in exporting commercial passenger aircraft to Iran and requires Treasury to assess sanctions risks, tightening oversight of Iran's access to finance.

members.bottom_line: Does not count: no anti-interventionist vote on aid to Israel (military aid to other countries: consistent (1 of 1 anti); sanctions: inconsistent (1 of 7 anti)) by this point. (Rule-based from Voteview roll calls.)

The bill also authorizes the President to designate and subject to sanctions any person who knowingly engages in specified activities with North Korea.
The FY2018 NDAA authorized defense appropriations, including Overseas Contingency Operations funding that supports U.S. military activities abroad.

Passed the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, imposing new sanctions on Iran, Russia, and North Korea for ballistic missile programs, human rights abuses, cyber activities, and other geopolitical reasons.
HR2810 passed, closing portions of the conference on the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018

The House passed the Otto Warmbier North Korea Nuclear Sanctions Act, imposing broad financial sanctions on entities doing business with North Korea and requiring the U.S. to oppose international financial assistance to governments that don't implement similar sanctions.

The House passed the Iran Ballistic Missiles and International Sanctions Enforcement Act, which imposes new sanctions on Iranian government agencies and foreign entities involved in Iran's ballistic missile program and conventional weapons transfers.
The bill requires Treasury to report on Iranian officials' assets and recommend additional sanctions to counter ballistic missile development.

The bill imposes reporting requirements on financial institutions involved in exporting commercial passenger aircraft to Iran and requires Treasury to assess sanctions risks, tightening oversight of Iran's access to finance.

The Senate voted to table (kill) a joint resolution that would have disapproved a proposed export of defense articles and services to the Government of Bahrain, allowing the arms sale to proceed.
The Senate voted to discharge a joint resolution directing the removal of U.S. armed forces from unauthorized hostilities in Yemen.
The Senate voted to proceed to a joint resolution directing the removal of U.S. armed forces from unauthorized hostilities in Yemen.
The amendment clarified that the Yemen war powers resolution prohibits U.S. armed forces from refueling non-U.S. aircraft conducting missions in Yemen's civil war.

Senate rejected an amendment to the Yemen War Powers Resolution (S.J.Res. 54) that would have exempted U.S. forces engaged in operations against Houthi attacks outside Yemen from the requirement to withdraw from unauthorized hostilities.
